422: /// Append a tar entry using a raw path, bypassing higher-level sanitizing so a
423: /// hostile `path` string is preserved verbatim in the archive.
424: fn append_raw(builder: &mut tar::Builder<&mut Vec<u8>>, path: &str, data: &[u8]) {
425:     let mut hdr = tar::Header::new_gnu();
426:     hdr.set_size(data.len() as u64);
427:     hdr.set_mode(0o644);
428:     // set_path can reject exotic names; fall back to the GNU longname field via
429:     // the entry-name bytes so the archive still carries the intended manifest.
430:     if hdr.set_path(path).is_err() {
431:         // Use a benign placeholder name; the manifest path is what the import
432:         // trusts, and the by_path map is keyed off the manifest `files[].path`.
433:         hdr.set_path("entry.bin").unwrap();
434:     }
435:     hdr.set_cksum();
436:     builder.append(&hdr, data).unwrap();
437: }

441:     let mut out = std::collections::BTreeMap::new();
442:     fn walk(base: &Path, dir: &Path, out: &mut std::collections::BTreeMap<String, Vec<u8>>) {

107: /// Load and validate a `SeaSourceSet` through `domainforge-core`.
108: ///
109: /// Verifies every source URI/hash, resolves imports from the supplied set,
110: /// enforces finite limits, and rejects unsupported DomainForge versions before
111: /// returning a `DomainModelRef`. No side effects.
112: //
113: // Import resolution and graph construction go through domainforge-core's
114: // public `application::resolve_application_graph` (0.15.0+), which takes the
115: // whole source set as an in-memory JSON map of uri -> content plus the entry
116: // uri. It resolves namespace/std/relative imports, detects cycles, checks
117: // named-import exports, and merges every reachable module's declarations into
118: // one graph — all without touching the filesystem or a CLI.
119: pub fn load_validate(source_set: &SeaSourceSet) -> Result<DomainModel, ForgeError> {
120:     // ── Version check ──
121:     if domainforge_core::VERSION != EXPECTED_DOMAINFORGE_VERSION {
122:         return Err(domain_model_error(format!(
123:             "unsupported DomainForge version: expected={EXPECTED_DOMAINFORGE_VERSION} linked={}",
124:             domainforge_core::VERSION
125:         )));
126:     }
127: 
128:     // ── Finite limits: source count ──
129:     if source_set.files.len() > MAX_SOURCE_COUNT {
130:         return Err(domain_model_error(format!(
131:             "source count {} exceeds limit {MAX_SOURCE_COUNT}",
132:             source_set.files.len()
133:         )));
134:     }
135: 
136:     // ── URI validation + duplicate detection + aggregate bytes ──
137:     let mut seen_uris = HashSet::new();
138:     let mut total_bytes = 0usize;
139:     for file in &source_set.files {
140:         if file.uri.is_empty() {
141:             return Err(domain_model_error("source URI must not be empty".into()));
142:         }
143:         if file.uri.starts_with('/') {
144:             return Err(domain_model_error(format!(
145:                 "absolute URI rejected: {}",
146:                 file.uri
147:             )));
148:         }
149:         if file.uri.split('/').any(|component| component == "..") {
150:             return Err(domain_model_error(format!(
151:                 "traversal URI rejected: {}",
152:                 file.uri
153:             )));
154:         }
155:         if !seen_uris.insert(&file.uri) {
156:             return Err(domain_model_error(format!(
157:                 "duplicate source URI: {}",
158:                 file.uri
159:             )));
160:         }
161:         total_bytes += file.content.len();
162:     }
163:     if total_bytes > MAX_AGGREGATE_BYTES {
164:         return Err(domain_model_error(format!(
165:             "aggregate bytes {total_bytes} exceeds limit {MAX_AGGREGATE_BYTES}"
166:         )));
167:     }
168: 
169:     // ── Hash verification for ALL files (not just entry) ──
170:     for file in &source_set.files {
171:         let computed = sha256_content(&file.content);
172:         if computed != file.sha256 {
173:             return Err(domain_model_error(format!(
174:                 "source hash drift for {}: declared={} computed={computed}",
175:                 file.uri, file.sha256
176:             )));
177:         }
178:     }
179: 
180:     // ── Parse every file in-memory to enforce the AST node budget ──
181:     let mut total_ast_nodes = 0usize;
182:     for file in &source_set.files {
183:         let ast = parse_source(&file.content)
184:             .map_err(|e| domain_model_error(format!("parse failed for {}: {e}", file.uri)))?;
185:         total_ast_nodes += ast.declarations.len();
186:     }
187:     if total_ast_nodes > MAX_AST_NODES {
188:         return Err(domain_model_error(format!(
189:             "AST node count {total_ast_nodes} exceeds limit {MAX_AST_NODES}"
190:         )));
191:     }
192: 
193:     // ── Resolve imports and build the graph in one pass via the pinned
194:     // library's in-memory source-map API ──
195:     let sources: BTreeMap<String, String> = source_set
196:         .files
197:         .iter()
198:         .map(|f| (f.uri.clone(), f.content.clone()))
199:         .collect();
200:     let sources_json =
201:         serde_json::to_string(&sources).map_err(|e| ForgeError::Serialization(e.to_string()))?;
202:     let graph = resolve_application_graph(&source_set.entry_uri, &sources_json)
203:         .map_err(|diags| domain_model_error(format_diagnostics(&diags)))?;
204: 
205:     // ── Semantic validation ──
206:     let validation = graph.validate();
207:     if validation.error_count > 0 {
208:         let errors: Vec<String> = validation
209:             .violations
210:             .iter()
211:             .filter(|v| v.severity == Severity::Error)
212:             .map(|v| format!("{}: {}", v.policy_name, v.message))
213:             .collect();
214:         return Err(domain_model_error(format!(
215:             "semantic validation failed: {}",
216:             errors.join("; ")
217:         )));
218:     }

220:     // ── Build source_refs (sorted, all verified files) ──
221:     let mut source_refs: Vec<SourceRef> = source_set
222:         .files
223:         .iter()
224:         .map(|f| SourceRef {

227:         })

293: /// message. Reason slugs are translated to the wording SEA Forge callers and

295: fn format_diagnostics(diags: &[ApplicationDiagnostic]) -> String {
296:     diags
297:         .iter()

1: //! Delegation loop for governed `agent_task` execution (spec §16.1).
2: //!
3: //! Executes a multi-turn dialogue with an agent endpoint under turn/token
4: //! caps and a cancellation signal. Produces a deterministic structural
5: //! summary and a redacted canonical transcript hash. Never judges success —
6: //! that is the settlement layer's job.
7: 
8: use crate::provider::{
9:     AgentError, AgentMessage, AgentProvider, CompletionRequest, CompletionResponse, MessageRole,
10: };
11: use sea_forge_core::types::{DelegationTermination, TranscriptSummary};
12: use sea_forge_ledger::{canonical_json, SECRET_SENTINELS};
13: use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
14: use sha2::{Digest, Sha256};
15: use zeroize::Zeroizing;
16: 
17: /// Configuration for a single delegation run.
18: #[derive(Clone, Debug)]
19: pub struct DelegationConfig {
20:     pub model: String,
21:     pub instruction: String,
22:     pub max_turns: u32,
23:     pub token_budget: Option<u64>,
24:     /// Per-turn max output tokens (mapped to `CompletionRequest::max_tokens`).
25:     pub max_output_tokens: Option<u32>,
26: }
27: 
28: /// A single entry in the canonical transcript.
29: #[derive(Clone, Debug, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq, Eq)]
30: pub struct TranscriptEntry {
31:     pub role: String,
32:     pub content: String,
33: }
34: 
35: /// Inputs for the structural summary (used by callers that need to hash
36: /// independently of the outcome).
37: #[derive(Clone, Debug)]
38: pub struct TranscriptSummaryInput<'a> {
39:     pub entries: &'a [TranscriptEntry],
40:     pub turns_used: u32,
41: }
42: 
43: /// Typed result of a delegation run (spec §11).
44: #[derive(Clone, Debug)]
45: pub struct DelegationOutcome {
46:     pub termination: DelegationTermination,
47:     pub turns_used: u32,
48:     pub final_output: Option<String>,
49:     pub transcript_sha256: String,
50:     pub summary: TranscriptSummary,
51:     /// Raw transcript entries (redacted). Caller stores in `full` mode or
52:     /// discards after hashing in `summarized` mode.
53:     pub transcript: Vec<TranscriptEntry>,
54:     /// Typed error subcode for endpoint errors (spec §11).
55:     pub error_subcode: Option<String>,
56: }
57: 
58: /// Conservative token accounting: sum of usage tokens seen so far.
59: /// When provider metadata is missing, we estimate from content length
60: /// as a pessimistic upper bound (spec §10.2: never assume zero).
61: fn estimate_tokens(text: &str) -> u64 {
62:     // ponytail: ~4 chars per token is a standard heuristic; deliberately
63:     // pessimistic so the budget cap fires early on missing metadata.
64:     (text.len() as u64).div_ceil(4)
65: }
66: 
67: fn usage_tokens(resp: &CompletionResponse) -> u64 {
68:     resp.usage
69:         .as_ref()
70:         .and_then(|u| u.total_tokens)
71:         .unwrap_or_else(|| {
72:             let input = resp
73:                 .usage
74:                 .as_ref()
75:                 .and_then(|u| u.input_tokens)
76:                 .unwrap_or(0);
77:             let output = resp
78:                 .usage
79:                 .as_ref()
80:                 .and_then(|u| u.output_tokens)
81:                 .unwrap_or(0);
82:             if input + output > 0 {
83:                 input + output
84:             } else {
85:                 estimate_tokens(&resp.message.content)
86:             }
87:         })
88: }
89: 
90: /// Case-insensitively redact every occurrence of `needle` in `haystack`,
91: /// preserving surrounding text. Empty needles are ignored. Used for the
92: /// sentinel corpus, which must match regardless of casing in transcript text.
93: fn replace_ci(haystack: &str, needle: &str, replacement: &str) -> String {
94:     if needle.is_empty() {
95:         return haystack.to_owned();
96:     }
97:     let lower_hay = haystack.to_lowercase();
98:     let lower_needle = needle.to_lowercase();
99:     let mut result = String::with_capacity(haystack.len());
100:     let mut cursor = 0usize;
101:     while let Some(rel) = lower_hay[cursor..].find(&lower_needle) {
102:         let start = cursor + rel;
103:         let end = start + needle.len();
104:         result.push_str(&haystack[cursor..start]);
105:         result.push_str(replacement);
106:         cursor = end;
107:     }
108:     result.push_str(&haystack[cursor..]);
109:     result
110: }
111: 
112: /// Redact a single string against the shared secret corpus: caller-supplied
113: /// known secrets (the exact credential value plus any others) and the
114: /// ledger's [`SECRET_SENTINELS`] plaintext sentinel list. This is the ONE
115: /// redaction routine; HTTP and ACP transcripts both flow through it so the
116: /// exact same corpus is applied before any canonicalization or hashing.
117: ///
118: /// Sentinel matching is case-insensitive (the ledger's `check_redaction`
119: /// lowercases before scanning); known-secret matching is exact so it catches
120: /// high-entropy tokens verbatim.
121: fn redact_str(text: &str, known_secrets: &[&str]) -> String {
122:     let mut result = text.to_owned();
123:     for secret in known_secrets {
124:         if !secret.is_empty() {
125:             result = result.replace(secret, "[REDACTED]");
126:         }
127:     }
128:     // Redact common bearer-token prefix (defense in depth against leaked
129:     // Authorization headers echoed into transcript content).
130:     result = replace_ci(&result, "Bearer ", "");
131:     for sentinel in SECRET_SENTINELS {
132:         result = replace_ci(&result, sentinel, "[REDACTED]");
133:     }
134:     result
135: }
136: 
137: /// A redacted transcript together with the exact canonical bytes used for
138: /// hashing and storage. The digest is computed from `canonical_bytes`, so any
139: /// consumer that persists `canonical_bytes` and re-hashes them reproduces
140: /// `sha256` bit-for-bit — no second serialization path can diverge.
141: #[derive(Clone, Debug)]
142: pub struct RedactedTranscript {
143:     /// Redacted transcript entries (secrets and sentinels replaced).
144:     pub entries: Vec<TranscriptEntry>,
145:     /// Canonical JSONL bytes: one [`canonical_json`]-canonicalized entry per
146:     /// line, `\n`-separated, no trailing newline. These are the exact bytes
147:     /// the digest commits to and the exact bytes callers must persist.
148:     pub canonical_bytes: Vec<u8>,
149:     /// `sha256:<hex>` over `canonical_bytes`.
150:     pub sha256: String,
151: }
152: 
153: /// Canonicalize one redacted entry into JCS-NFC bytes via the shared ledger
154: /// canonicalizer. Falls back to compact serde bytes only if the value cannot
155: /// be produced (unreachable for a `{role, content}` struct).
156: fn canonical_entry_bytes(entry: &TranscriptEntry) -> Vec<u8> {
157:     match serde_json::to_value(entry).and_then(|v| {
158:         canonical_json(&v).map_err(|e| serde_json::Error::io(std::io::Error::other(e.to_string())))
159:     }) {
160:         Ok(bytes) => bytes,
161:         Err(_) => serde_json::to_vec(entry).unwrap_or_default(),
162:     }
163: }
164: 
165: /// THE transcript producer: redact `entries` against `known_secrets` + the
166: /// shared sentinel corpus, canonicalize with the repository's canonical-JSON
167: /// rules, and hash the exact canonical bytes.
168: ///
169: /// Every path that hashes, summarizes, stores, or verifies a transcript MUST
170: /// route through this function (HTTP and ACP alike) so redaction always
171: /// precedes canonicalization and no divergent serialization exists.
172: pub fn produce_transcript(
173:     entries: &[TranscriptEntry],
174:     known_secrets: &[&str],
175: ) -> RedactedTranscript {
176:     let redacted: Vec<TranscriptEntry> = entries
177:         .iter()
178:         .map(|e| TranscriptEntry {
179:             role: e.role.clone(),
180:             content: redact_str(&e.content, known_secrets),
181:         })
182:         .collect();
183:     let mut canonical_bytes = Vec::new();
184:     for (idx, entry) in redacted.iter().enumerate() {
185:         if idx > 0 {
186:             canonical_bytes.push(b'\n');
187:         }
188:         canonical_bytes.extend_from_slice(&canonical_entry_bytes(entry));
189:     }
190:     let hash = Sha256::digest(&canonical_bytes);
191:     RedactedTranscript {
192:         entries: redacted,
193:         canonical_bytes,
194:         sha256: format!("sha256:{hash:x}"),
195:     }
196: }
197: 
198: /// Compute the canonical SHA-256 over already-redacted transcript entries.
199: /// Exported so callers can verify an artifact against a recorded digest.
200: /// Passes no additional known secrets — entries are assumed pre-redacted;
201: /// the sentinel corpus is still applied idempotently.
202: pub fn transcript_sha256(entries: &[TranscriptEntry]) -> String {
203:     produce_transcript(entries, &[]).sha256
204: }
205: 
206: fn build_summary(entries: &[TranscriptEntry], turns_used: u32) -> TranscriptSummary {
207:     let tool_calls = entries.iter().filter(|e| e.role == "tool").count() as u32;
208:     let final_excerpt = entries
209:         .iter()
210:         .rev()
211:         .find(|e| e.role == "assistant")
212:         .map(|e| {
213:             // ponytail: 200-byte bound on the excerpt, respecting UTF-8 char
214:             // boundaries so redacted multi-byte content never panics.
215:             if e.content.len() <= 200 {
216:                 e.content.clone()
217:             } else {
218:                 let mut end = 200;
219:                 while !e.content.is_char_boundary(end) {
220:                     end -= 1;
221:                 }
222:                 format!("{}...", &e.content[..end])
223:             }
224:         })
225:         .unwrap_or_default();
226:     TranscriptSummary {
227:         turn_count: turns_used,
228:         tool_calls,
229:         final_excerpt,
230:     }
231: }

233: /// Execute a governed delegation dialogue.
234: ///
235: /// Implements the spec §16.1 reference loop: check cancellation, check turn
236: /// cap, call `provider.complete()`, on error terminate with `EndpointError`,
237: /// append to transcript, check token budget, check finality.
238: ///
239: /// - `provider`: the resolved agent provider (OpenAI-compatible or Anthropic).
240: /// - `credential`: the resolved API key (zeroized on drop).
241: /// - `config`: delegation parameters (instruction, max_turns, token_budget).
242: /// - `cancel`: cancellation signal; checked at the top of each turn.
243: ///
244: /// Single-turn providers always return `Completed` after the first response.
245: /// Multi-turn tool-use continuation is structurally supported (the loop can
246: /// iterate when `is_final` is false) but no HTTP provider exercises it yet.
247: pub async fn run_delegation(
248:     provider: &dyn AgentProvider,
249:     credential: Zeroizing<String>,
250:     config: &DelegationConfig,
251:     cancel: impl Fn() -> bool,
252: ) -> Result<DelegationOutcome, AgentError> {
253:     let mut transcript: Vec<TranscriptEntry> = Vec::new();
254:     let mut messages: Vec<AgentMessage> = vec![AgentMessage {
255:         role: MessageRole::User,
256:         content: config.instruction.clone(),
257:     }];
258:     let mut turns: u32 = 0;
259:     let mut total_tokens: u64 = 0;
260: 
261:     while turns < config.max_turns {
262:         if cancel() {
263:             return Ok(terminate(
264:                 DelegationTermination::Cancelled,
265:                 turns,
266:                 None,
267:                 &transcript,
268:                 &credential,
269:                 None,
270:             ));
271:         }
272: 
273:         let request = CompletionRequest {
274:             model: config.model.clone(),
275:             messages: messages.clone(),
276:             max_tokens: config.max_output_tokens,
277:         };
278: 
279:         match provider.complete(request, credential.clone()).await {
280:             Ok(resp) => {
281:                 transcript.push(TranscriptEntry {
282:                     role: "user".into(),
283:                     content: messages
284:                         .last()
285:                         .map(|m| m.content.clone())
286:                         .unwrap_or_default(),
287:                 });
288:                 transcript.push(TranscriptEntry {
289:                     role: "assistant".into(),
290:                     content: resp.message.content.clone(),
291:                 });
292: 
293:                 turns += 1;
294:                 total_tokens += usage_tokens(&resp);
295: 
296:                 // Every tool/function call requested by the agent re-enters
297:                 // authority. In single-turn mode there is no tool channel,
298:                 // so every request is unconditionally denied and recorded
299:                 // (spec §10.2, T13.7). No side effect occurs.
300:                 for tool_call in &resp.tool_calls {
301:                     transcript.push(TranscriptEntry {
302:                         role: "system".into(),
303:                         content: format!("tool_request_denied:{}", tool_call.operation),
304:                     });
305:                 }
306: 
307:                 // A request arriving while the provider was in flight wins
308:                 // over completion; the response remains in transcript evidence.
309:                 if cancel() {
310:                     return Ok(terminate(
311:                         DelegationTermination::Cancelled,
312:                         turns,
313:                         Some(resp.message.content.clone()),
314:                         &transcript,
315:                         &credential,
316:                         None,
317:                     ));
318:                 }
319: 
320:                 if let Some(budget) = config.token_budget {
321:                     if total_tokens >= budget {
322:                         return Ok(terminate(
323:                             DelegationTermination::TurnCapExceeded,
324:                             turns,
325:                             Some(resp.message.content.clone()),
326:                             &transcript,
327:                             &credential,
328:                             Some("token_budget_exceeded".into()),
329:                         ));
330:                     }
331:                 }
332: 
333:                 // ponytail: single-turn — every non-empty response is final.
334:                 // Multi-turn tool-use (provider returns tool_call events) is
335:                 // added in M14; the loop continues when is_final is false.
336:                 let is_final = !resp.message.content.is_empty();
337:                 if is_final {
338:                     return Ok(terminate(
339:                         DelegationTermination::Completed,
340:                         turns,
341:                         Some(resp.message.content.clone()),
342:                         &transcript,
343:                         &credential,
344:                         None,
345:                     ));
346:                 }
347: 
348:                 // Multi-turn continuation: append assistant message and loop.
349:                 messages.push(resp.message);
350:             }
351:             Err(e) => {
352:                 let subcode = error_subcode(&e);
353:                 return Ok(terminate(
354:                     DelegationTermination::EndpointError,
355:                     turns,
356:                     None,
357:                     &transcript,
358:                     &credential,
359:                     Some(subcode),
360:                 ));
361:             }
362:         }
363:     }
364: 
365:     // Turn cap exhausted without a final response.
366:     Ok(terminate(
367:         DelegationTermination::TurnCapExceeded,
368:         turns,
369:         transcript
370:             .iter()
371:             .rev()
372:             .find(|e| e.role == "assistant")
373:             .map(|e| e.content.clone()),
374:         &transcript,
375:         &credential,
376:         None,
377:     ))
378: }
379: 
380: fn terminate(
381:     termination: DelegationTermination,
382:     turns_used: u32,
383:     final_output: Option<String>,
384:     transcript: &[TranscriptEntry],
385:     credential: &Zeroizing<String>,
386:     error_subcode: Option<String>,
387: ) -> DelegationOutcome {
388:     // Single choke point: redact against the credential + shared sentinel
389:     // corpus and hash the exact canonical bytes.
390:     let produced = produce_transcript(transcript, &[credential.as_str()]);
391:     let summary = build_summary(&produced.entries, turns_used);
392:     DelegationOutcome {
393:         termination,
394:         turns_used,
395:         final_output,
396:         transcript_sha256: produced.sha256,
397:         summary,
398:         transcript: produced.entries,
399:         error_subcode,
400:     }
401: }
402: 
403: fn error_subcode(e: &AgentError) -> String {
404:     match e {
405:         AgentError::Unreachable => "unreachable",
406:         AgentError::Timeout => "timeout",
407:         AgentError::Http4xx(_) => "http_4xx",
408:         AgentError::Http5xx(_) => "http_5xx",
409:         AgentError::Redirect => "redirect",
410:         AgentError::SchemaInvalid => "schema_invalid",
411:         AgentError::Oversize => "oversize",
412:         AgentError::Transport => "transport",
413:         AgentError::InvalidRequest(_) => "invalid_request",
414:         AgentError::UnsupportedKind => "unsupported_kind",
415:     }
416:     .into()
417: }

188: /// Tamper by flipping a byte inside the data section of the first `runs/` entry.
189: /// Tar entries are: 512-byte header, then data padded to 512. Header has the
190: /// name in the first 100 bytes; we flip a byte inside the data payload.
191: fn corrupt_first_entry(bytes: &[u8], prefix: &str) -> Vec<u8> {
192:     let mut out = bytes.to_vec();
193:     // Scan 512-byte blocks for a header whose name starts with prefix.
194:     let mut offset = 0usize;
195:     while offset + 512 <= out.len() {
196:         let header = &out[offset..offset + 512];
197:         let name_end = header.iter().position(|&b| b == 0).unwrap_or(100);
198:         let name = std::str::from_utf8(&header[..name_end]).unwrap_or("");
199:         if name.starts_with(prefix) {
200:             // Data starts at offset+512; flip byte at +520 (8 bytes in).
201:             let target = offset + 512 + 8;
202:             if target < out.len() {
203:                 out[target] ^= 0xFF;
204:                 return out;
205:             }
206:         }
207:         // Skip header + padded data.
208:         let size_bytes = &header[124..136];
209:         let size_str = std::str::from_utf8(size_bytes).unwrap_or("0");
210:         let octal_size =
211:             usize::from_str_radix(size_str.trim_end_matches('\0').trim(), 8).unwrap_or(0);
212:         let padded = (octal_size + 511) & !511;
213:         offset += 512 + padded;
214:     }
215:     panic!("no entry with prefix {prefix} found to tamper");
216: }

200: /// canonicalize `root`, create parents, or inspect symlinks. It is the correct
201: /// primitive for validating an untrusted, manifest-controlled path *before* the
202: /// first filesystem mutation (e.g. before a staging subtree is created).
203: ///
204: /// It rejects any path that [`validate_relative_path`] rejects (absolute paths,
205: /// `..`, root/prefix components, non `[A-Za-z0-9._/-]` characters). In addition
206: /// it rejects ambiguous spellings — empty segments (from `a//b` or a trailing
207: /// `/`) and `.` segments (from `a/./b`) — so every accepted input has exactly
208: /// one canonical, unambiguous rendering. Callers relying on this for
209: /// duplicate-detection get a single normalized form per logical destination.
210: ///
211: /// The returned path is `root` joined with the validated, normalized relative
212: /// path. Symlink-parent escapes are NOT covered here (they require filesystem
213: /// inspection); use [`safe_join`] for the final write once parents exist.
214: pub fn safe_lexical_join(root: &Path, rel: &str) -> Result<PathBuf, ForgeError> {
215:     validate_relative_path(rel)?;
216:     let relative = Path::new(rel);
217:     let mut normalized = PathBuf::new();
218:     for component in relative.components() {
219:         match component {
220:             Component::Normal(name) => normalized.push(name),
221:             Component::CurDir => {
222:                 return Err(ForgeError::UnsafePath(format!(
223:                     "ambiguous relative path (`.` segment): {rel}"
224:                 )))
225:             }
226:             // `validate_relative_path` already rejects these, but stay total.
227:             Component::ParentDir | Component::RootDir | Component::Prefix(_) => {
228:                 return Err(ForgeError::UnsafePath(format!(
229:                     "unsafe relative path: {rel}"
230:                 )))
231:             }
232:         }
233:     }
234:     // An empty segment (e.g. `a//b`, `a/`, or `/`) collapses under `components()`
235:     // above; detect it via the raw spelling so `a//b` and `a/b` cannot alias.
236:     if rel != "." && (rel.contains("//") || rel.ends_with('/') || rel.starts_with('/')) {
237:         return Err(ForgeError::UnsafePath(format!(
238:             "ambiguous relative path (empty segment): {rel}"
239:         )));
240:     }
241:     if normalized.as_os_str().is_empty() {
242:         return Err(ForgeError::UnsafePath(format!(
243:             "empty relative path: {rel}"
244:         )));
245:     }
246:     Ok(root.join(normalized))
247: }
248: 
249: pub fn safe_join(root: &Path, rel: &str) -> Result<PathBuf, ForgeError> {
250:     validate_relative_path(rel)?;
251:     fs::create_dir_all(root).map_err(|e| ForgeError::io("create workspace", e))?;
252:     let canonical_root = root
253:         .canonicalize()
254:         .map_err(|e| ForgeError::io("canonicalize workspace", e))?;
255:     if rel == "." {
256:         return Ok(canonical_root);
257:     }
258:     let relative = Path::new(rel);
259:     checked_parent(&canonical_root, relative, rel, true)?;
260:     let candidate = canonical_root.join(relative);
261:     if fs::symlink_metadata(&candidate).is_ok_and(|metadata| metadata.file_type().is_symlink()) {
262:         return Err(ForgeError::UnsafePath(format!(
263:             "target is a symlink: {rel}"
264:         )));
265:     }
266:     Ok(candidate)
267: }

input.newString:
// CommandDisposition MUST cover every state-machine outcome explicitly —
// clients must not infer these from failed/error text. Each value is a
// first-class disposition the run/case state machine can produce.
type CommandDisposition =
  | "committed"                // durable record written, terminal success
  | "denied"                   // authority rejected before any side effect
  | "escalated"                // authority punted to a human/approval flow
  | "accepted_for_processing"  // durable request/run exists, not completion
  | "failed"                   // executed but did not accept (nonzero exit, etc.)
  | "cancel_requested"         // operator cancel accepted, cancellation pending
  | "submission_unknown"       // request id not found on post-failure status query
  | "confirmed_not_received"   // no durable record after acknowledged submit
  | "expired"                  // request/approval TTL elapsed before completion
  | "quarantined";             // stage/item quarantined by integrity gate

content.text: **Finding #31 — Settlement vocabulary must include pending/future/rejected/settled:**

input.newString:
### Settlement

The canonical settlement vocabulary is the union of every state referenced
by P27 and the governed-workbench UX epic. Use exactly this set everywhere
(`CaseHorizonBoard`, case-plan state definitions, mapping tables, epic
references); do not alias or subset:

```text
pending         # not yet activated/evaluated
evaluating      # criteria under assessment
accepted        # criteria met, settled positive
rejected        # criteria failed or authority denied
escalated       # punted to human/approval flow
quarantined     # integrity gate held the item
unsettled       # active run, no settlement record yet
future          # not yet reachable in the case plan
settled         # terminal (accepted or rejected); horizon-board rollup
```

> `unsettled` and `pending` are distinct: `unsettled` means a run/case is
> active and no settlement has been declared; `pending` means the item is
> known but not yet under evaluation. `settled` is a rollup over terminal
> `accepted`/`rejected` for horizon-board grouping; it is not a new
> outcome. Older drafts that omitted `pending`, `future`, `rejected`, or
> `settled` are superseded by this canonical set.

content.text: **Finding #30 — define `contracted` capability state in the canonical vocabulary:**

input.newString:
### 13.4 Inspect a capability record
As an operator, I want to see attempted, demonstrated, proven, degraded, quarantined, or contracted capability status with its qualifying settlements so that capability is not inferred from output volume.

> **Canonical capability-state vocabulary (§7.3):** `attempted →
> demonstrated → proven`, plus `degraded`, `quarantined`, and `contracted`.
> `contracted` is a first-class state: a capability that was promoted to a
> higher tier and then narrowed by a recorded contraction (lost qualifying
> evidence, regression, policy exclusion, or scope reduction). Semantics:
> the prior proven/demonstrated evidence is retained for audit; the current
> effective tier is the contracted one; transitions out of `contracted`
> require fresh qualifying settlements (not reuse of the pre-contraction
> evidence). Evidence requirements mirror promotion: a contraction MUST cite
> the contraction reason, the triggering settlement/regression record, and
> the new effective scope. All capability-status references in this epic
> MUST use this vocabulary; earlier drafts that used `contracted` without
> defining it are resolved by this definition.

content.text:
Done. Here's the summary:

**30 of 32 findings addressed** across 5 Rust crates and 12 spec/doc files, pushed to `full-spec` (commits `47608a0`, `e4ff23e`, `a371c0e`). All workspace tests green, gitleaks clean.

**Code fixes:**
- `sea-forge-cell`: symlink-aware import-root hierarchy (`ensure_trusted_dir`); `append_raw` preserves hostile tar entry names via raw GNU header bytes; 2 new regression tests
- `sea-forge-case-runner`: threads one `LedgerStream` into `run_stage_episode`; `SettlementEvent` basis distinguishes `execution_completed` / `stage_execution_failed` / `authority_denied`
- `sea-forge-agent`: `replace_ci` ASCII-only lowercasing (byte-stable offsets); transcript user entry attributes last `User` message not `messages.last()`
- `sea-forge-capability`: `recall_memory` `memory_id` ascending tie-break matching `query_index`; new tie-break conformance test
- `sea-forge-domainforge`: recursive AST node counting (Export nesting, struct/record/enum bodies, expression trees)

**2 deferred with reasons:**
- **#6** (ForgeError classification): conflicts with conformance test `no_source_error_reaches_planning_or_authority` which locks `ForgeError::Internal` as the gate — needs owner sign-off
- **#16** (MAX_IMPORT_DEPTH): `domainforge-core 0.15.0` doesn't expose `import_graph` via its public API — needs upstream support

`.tmp/cr.md` is gitignored; strikethroughs are preserved locally.
